_meta.geography: San Francisco Bay Area / Silicon Valley, USA
_meta.note: Every number used anywhere in the notebook is declared here with a source, an as-of date and a confidence tier. Tier A = primary filing / government release. Tier B = large reputable private dataset. Tier C = secondary reporting or practitioner benchmark; treat as indicative only.

confidence_tiers.A: Primary source: SEC filing, BLS/IRS/EDD release, or a survey publisher's own report.
confidence_tiers.B: Large private dataset published by the data owner (levels.fyi, KFF, Carta, Vanguard, Cushman & Wakefield).
confidence_tiers.C: Secondary reporting, practitioner benchmark, or a derived estimate. Wide error bars.

levels_fyi_bay_area_swe_all_levels.source: levels.fyi — Software Engineer Salary in San Francisco Bay Area
levels_fyi_bay_area_swe_all_levels.note: Self-reported, verification-encouraged. Skews toward large public tech employers and toward people who are happy with their offer; treat the median as an upper-ish estimate of the true Bay Area market median.

levels_fyi_google_bay_area_swe_by_level.source: levels.fyi — Google Software Engineer Salary, San Francisco Bay Area
levels_fyi_google_bay_area_swe_by_level.note: 'stock' is levels.fyi's FIRST-YEAR stock number, which for a front-loaded vest can exceed the annualised grant value. Company-wide submission count is 23,589 across all locations.

levels_fyi_peer_benchmarks.unit: USD annual total compensation, SF Bay Area
levels_fyi_peer_benchmarks.source: levels.fyi company pages (Scale AI n=181, Amazon)

bls_ecec.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics — Employer Costs for Employee Compensation, June 2026, Table 4
bls_ecec.unit: USD per hour worked / percent of total compensation
bls_ecec.note: This is the national benchmark the whole model is calibrated against. For professional occupations, benefits are 30.8% of total compensation, i.e. a 44.5% load on wages. BLS counts paid leave and supplemental pay as 'benefits'; in a salaried tech job those are already inside the salary and bonus lines, so the notebook excludes them to avoid double-counting.

social_security.note: Wage base resets per employer; a mid-year hire who already hit the cap elsewhere still costs the new employer the full 6.2% up to $184,500.

medicare.note: No cap. The additional 0.9% Medicare surtax above $200k is EMPLOYEE-paid, not an employer cost.

futa.california_2026_status: unsettled until the November 2026 IRS credit-reduction notice
futa.source: IRS FUTA credit reduction states; California payroll guidance
futa.note: California has been a credit-reduction state. 2025 ran at a 1.2% reduction => 1.8% effective. Sources disagree on 2026 (0.3% to 5.3% cited); the model defaults to 1.8% and sweeps 0.6%-2.7%.

ca_sui.note: Only the first $7,000 of wages, so this is a flat ~$238 per head at the new-employer rate, not a percentage of a $200k salary.

ca_sdi.note: EMPLOYEE-paid in California. Included here only so it is explicitly excluded from the employer cost model — it is a common double-count.

workers_compensation.source: Practitioner benchmark for CA class code 8810 (clerical) / 8859 (software development)
workers_compensation.note: Low-hazard office class codes. Rates vary by carrier, experience mod and payroll size.

irs_401a17_comp_limit_2026.source: IRS 2026 cost-of-living adjustments as summarised by benefits counsel (Mayer Brown, Venable, Plante Moran)
irs_401a17_comp_limit_2026.note: Caps the compensation on which a 401(k) match can be computed. Up from $350,000 in 2025.

kff_2025_premiums.note: National averages. Employer share is total premium minus worker contribution. The notebook trends these forward one year at the surveyed growth rate and applies a Bay Area / tech-employer uplift, because SV employers buy richer plans and cover more of the dependent premium.

bay_area_tech_premium_uplift.source: Derived: California Health Benefits Survey 2025 (CHCF) plus typical SV plan-richness and dependent-coverage practice

vanguard_401k_match.source: Vanguard, How America Saves 2025 (via PLANSPONSOR / PlanAdviser coverage)
vanguard_401k_match.note: This is the PROMISED match. Realised employer cost is lower because not every employee defers enough to capture the full match. The model applies a capture rate.

match_capture_rate.note: Share of the promised match actually paid out, after non-participants and under-deferrers. High in SV tech because of auto-enrolment and high pay.

ancillary_annual_employer_cost.note: Practitioner benchmarks for a Bay Area tech employer, blended across single/family tiers. Each is a point estimate with wide error bars; the Monte Carlo section varies them.

parental_leave.note: Cost modelled as weeks x weekly salary x the share of the workforce taking leave in a given year. Unlike most benefits this scales with salary.

ca_pto_accrual_liability.note: California requires accrued, unused vacation to be paid out at termination, so an accruing PTO balance is a real growing liability. Unlimited-PTO policies avoid the accrual but are not free — they trade the liability for higher average days taken.

immigration_sponsorship.note: H-1B filing plus counsel, or a green-card process (PERM + I-140 + I-485). Amortised over expected tenure in the model.

cost_per_hire.note: Mean is far above median because agency-sourced hires dominate the tail. For a Bay Area senior engineer the agency path is more representative.

agency_fee_pct_of_base.note: Contingency search for engineering in the Bay Area. Retained executive search runs higher.

sf_office_asking_rent_psf.unit: USD per square foot per year, gross
sf_office_asking_rent_psf.source: Cushman & Wakefield MarketBeat San Francisco Office Q3 2026; Savills Market in Minutes Q3 2026; Kidder Mathews
sf_office_asking_rent_psf.note: Publishers disagree mainly because of lease basis (gross vs full-service-gross) and submarket mix. 29.3% vacancy means effective rents after concessions are materially below asking.

sqft_per_employee.note: Post-hybrid densities. Pre-2020 benchmarks of 250-300 sqft are no longer representative.

annual_other_opex_per_employee.note: Practitioner benchmarks for a Bay Area software engineer.

span_of_control.note: Used only for the OPTIONAL allocated-management-overhead view, which is an allocation, not an incremental cash cost.

sec_filings.source: SEC EDGAR XBRL company facts (us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation, us-gaap:Revenues) and 10-K human capital disclosures

Meta.employees_source_quote: We had a global workforce of 78,865 employees as of December 31, 2025

sec_filings.note: SBC and revenue figures pulled directly from SEC XBRL facts. Headcount is not an XBRL fact; Meta's is quoted verbatim from the FY2025 10-K, the others are from company disclosure as reported. SBC-per-employee is a derived ratio, not a disclosed number, and it includes founder/executive mega-grants, so the mean sits well above the median employee's grant.

carta_tenure.source: Carta — Employment tenure statistics for startup companies
carta_tenure.note: Carta's own page reports a ~50% chance of departure by month 37, which sits just inside a 4-year vest. The commonly repeated '40% reach full vesting' figure is secondary and unverified against Carta's own pages.

vesting_structure.source: Carta vesting guide and secondary roundups (sources disagree: 85% vs 94%)

exercise_window.source: Secondary roundup attributing to Pave (2025); unverified against the primary report
exercise_window.note: Treat as indicative only. Extended (7-10 year) windows are increasingly common and materially change this number.

startup_survival.source: Carta — startup shutdown and graduation-rate data
startup_survival.note: Shutdown counts are Carta customers only, not a population rate. Graduation rates are a poor proxy for 'equity ends up worth something' but are the best published anchor.

replacement_cost_pct_of_salary.source: SHRM and Work Institute practitioner benchmarks
replacement_cost_pct_of_salary.note: Covers recruiting, lost productivity during vacancy, ramp time of the replacement, and the drag on the team. Higher for senior/specialist roles.

ramp_to_full_productivity_months.note: For a mid-to-senior engineer in a large codebase. The model charges the ramp period as a partial-productivity loss in year one.
